Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

sideview 0.7.0

Merging SUPP– tables

  • Merge into AE. A tagged SUPPAE, SUPPDM or SUPPQUAL card gets a Merge into button. It adds a merge step that folds the qualifier rows into the parent as one column per QNAM, with its QLABEL as the column label ("" when there is none). The step writes tidyr + dplyr code with guards that stop when the data no longer fits. Pressing the button again replaces the step, and one undo takes it back. A SUPPQUAL with several RDOMAINs gets one merge per parent on the canvas.
  • Merge check. The Discrepancy tab shows parent, SUPP, matched and orphan counts, rows of other RDOMAINs, a QNAM that repeats for one record, a clash with a parent column, a QNAM at two IDVAR levels, IDVARVAL values that do not convert (counted apart from orphans), the new columns and a 5-row preview. The step line in the Pipeline tab carries a one-line summary.
  • Refresh. When a re-check finds that the data no longer fit the plan (for example after editing suppae), the step reads “Merge needs refreshing” and Refresh takes the plan that check found, as one undo step (Refresh itself runs no new check).
  • Auto Map offers a SUPP card’s merge as a dashed spline group to its parent; accepting it adds the merge step instead of a join. The join check mentions the merge when you join a SUPP table by hand.
  • Lazy cards. An arrow or duckdb parent stays lazy; only the SUPP table is collected.
  • sv_supp_check() (new, exported) runs the merge check on two data frames or cards. sv_supp_check_json() and sv_supp_key_type() are exported with it. sv_suggest_mappings() gains rows with kind = "supp".
  • New Shiny wire items: the input supp_check_request ({id, parent, supp, plan?, rdomain?}) and the message sideview_supp_check.

Edge cases fixed in the merge

  • An IDVARVAL such as 1e999 (too large for a number) is now counted as “does not convert”, not as an orphan, and no longer stops the generated code on an Arrow int64 parent.
  • A missing QNAM is read as the text NA in the gadget and the widget alike (the merged column is named NA).
  • On a duckdb parent, records whose USUBJID or STUDYID is NA now receive their qualifiers, as the check says they do.
  • A float32 parent key is compared as the double it holds (0.1 stored as float32 is not "0.1"): such rows are orphans in the check, and the generated Arrow code no longer rounds them onto the parent.
  • On an Arrow parent with a narrow or decimal key (int8, int16, decimal), the generated code drops supp keys that the parent’s type cannot hold exactly. Before, 300 on int8 wrapped onto another record, and 0.125 on decimal(10, 2) was rounded onto one. The check already called such rows orphans.
  • A lazy SUPPQUAL with three or more RDOMAINs now offers a merge for every one, as in memory (only the first two were seen before). The default RDOMAIN is the first in byte order (AE before CM), the same in any locale and on every backend.
  • Only ASCII whitespace around a numeric IDVARVAL is ignored, as R does. A no-break space, BOM or ideographic space makes the value “does not convert”, in the gadget and the widget alike (the widget ignored them before).
  • A double IDVARVAL past 1e308 “does not convert” in the gadget and the widget alike. Before, R and the widget disagreed at the very top of the range.
  • With both a missing QNAM and a QNAM of "NA", the generated code now treats them as one name, as the check does.
  • A full-precision IDVARVAL of a float32 key (0.10000000149011612) matches in the lazy check as it does in memory.
  • An Arrow int64 key is a double key whatever its values (as a duckdb BIGINT already was), so a key past 2^31 no longer reads as “does not convert” on Arrow.

Limits to know about

  • The merge needs the exact upper-case column names USUBJID, IDVAR, IDVARVAL, QNAM and QVAL.
  • A second merge into one parent is checked for clashes in the browser; the guard in the generated code checks the source parent table only.
  • The check runs when you press the Merge button, open the step line or report, open a workspace, undo or redo, and after a module card is replaced or removed; Refresh runs none. Only the guards in the code stop a rerun on new data.
  • A double key with more than 15 significant digits can match differently: the in-memory R check compares 15-significant-digit text, while the generated code and the lazy duckdb check compare the doubles, so the gadget’s own report can disagree with its code for such keys (and the widget reads the shortest round-trip text).
  • With an arrow parent the code casts a numeric key to the parent’s Arrow type (an int64 parquet column joins); the clash guard reads the parent’s columns with collect(head(x, 0)), so arrow queries work.
  • A re-check sends the step’s RDOMAIN, so a step loaded with cdisc = FALSE, or after a tag changed, keeps its domain.
  • RELREC tables are still not merged or suggested.
  • A float16 parent key is not supported (Arrow cannot create float16 columns).
  • A double key beyond 1e308 is always “does not convert”, on purpose: R and JavaScript read the largest doubles differently.
  • At most 1000 RDOMAINs are read from a lazy SUPPQUAL.

sideview 0.6.0

CDISC join keys

  • Auto Map knows CDISC keys. For tables tagged SDTM, SEND or ADaM it suggests the keys a study programmer would use, instead of guessing from column names:
    • ADaM to SDTM trace: STUDYID, USUBJID and <D>SEQ (adae to ae by AESEQ).
    • Subject level: STUDYID + USUBJID, with DM (SDTM, SEND) or ADSL (ADaM) as the lookup table.
    • Visit level: a table with VISITNUM to SV, by the subject key and VISITNUM. Where a table has no STUDYID, the subject key is USUBJID alone, and the reason says so.
  • One click, one join, one undo. A key set is drawn as a group of dashed splines (class sideview-spline-suggested-cdisc). Hovering one lights up the group, and a click accepts all of it as one left_join (one undo step). A partial key set is never offered, because it would give a many-to-many join.
  • Key checks in the join check. The join check panel gets a “CDISC” note list: a missing key for a pair with a rule (Add AESEQ: ...), a many-to-many join with no rule (for example two Findings tables), and a natural key that repeats (STUDYID, USUBJID, AESEQ should identify one AE record, but 3 keys repeat). The notes are worked out in R, so they appear in the gadget and in Shiny modules; the widget has none.
  • sv_cdisc_join_keys(cards) (new, exported) returns the suggested key sets for a list of cards.
  • sv_suggest_mappings() gains the columns group and kind (both NA for heuristic rows) and a cdisc argument ("auto", FALSE or a named vector, as in sv_codebook()). Rule rows come first with confidence 1 and are never dropped by min_confidence. Between two tagged tables the old DOMAIN and lone-STUDYID guesses are gone.

Limits to know about

  • SUPP-- and RELREC tables are not suggested as joins (folding them into their parent is future work). Neither are tables without a USUBJID column (for example TS, TA, TE).
  • A sponsor sequence variable that is not called <D>SEQ is not traced; the pair still gets the subject rule.
  • Two Findings tables (LB with VS) get no suggestion, only a note: that join is many-to-many by nature.
  • The widget has no Auto Map rules and no key-check notes; they need R.
  • cdisc = FALSE turns the rules and the notes off.

sideview 0.5.0

CDISC awareness

  • Domain badges. Tables that look like SDTM, SEND or ADaM datasets get a small badge after the card name (DM, AE, ADSL, …). Hover for the dataset label, the standard and class, and why sideview thinks so. Supplemental qualifier tables (SUPPAE) say which parent they supplement. Other tables are never touched.

  • Variable labels. Column headers show a variable’s label as a tooltip, L shows a row of labels under the headers (saved with the workspace as view.labels_row), Ctrl+K also finds a card by its domain or dataset label, and the column inspector shows the label.

  • cdisc = on sideview(), sideview_widget(), save_sideview(), sideviewServer() and sv_codebook(): "auto" (default), FALSE, or a named vector such as c(my_ae = "AE"). Module canvases update their badges when a card is added or replaced.

  • sv_codebook() has a domain column. The widget’s CSV download matches it byte for byte.

  • sv_cdisc_catalogue() returns the dataset catalogue the detection uses.

  • sv_read_cdisc() reads a folder or a set of .xpt, .sas7bdat, Dataset-JSON and .parquet files into a named list for sideview(), keeping variable labels. Nothing goes over the network.

  • Copilot. The schema text sent to the LLM now includes column labels and a domain line. Row data is still never sent.

  • Overrides. A table you tag yourself (cdisc = c(my_adae = "ADAE")) gets the same class as an auto-detected one: ADaM tags take BDS, OCCDS, TTE or ADSL from the table’s columns, and SUPPAE-style tags get Relationship and their parent. On a SEND canvas an auto-detected SUPP table is SEND too; your own tags are never flipped. The hover text says why a table is SEND. Names in cdisc = ignore a file extension ("lab.csv" names the table lab); case still matters.

  • Codebook and canvas agree. The gadget’s codebook uses the badges on the canvas, so a tag you cleared stays cleared in the CSV. Labels sent to the Copilot are cut to 200 characters.

Limits to know about

  • The ig_versions column of the catalogue (SDTM, SEND and ADaM implementation guide versions) is approximate. It is for awareness, not conformance checking: sideview does not validate a dataset against an implementation guide.
  • A table named AD... (ADLB, ADAE, ADVS) whose columns confirm an ADaM structure is tagged ADaM even when it keeps SDTM-prefixed columns (LBTESTCD, AETERM, …); the tooltip notes the prefix as a disagreement. A table with any other name and SDTM-prefixed columns is still tagged by its prefix.
  • Column names are matched whatever their case (STUDYID, studyid, StudyID), so tables cleaned with janitor::clean_names() are still recognised. A STUDYID column is still required.
  • sideview_server(cdisc =), used with your own sideview_ui(), only sets the domain column of the codebook; the badges come from the cards given to sideview_ui().
  • sv_read_cdisc() skips a file found by scanning a folder, with one warning, when its reading package is not installed; a file named explicitly is still an error.
  • cdisc = FALSE shows no tags but, for lazy (arrow / duckdb) cards, detection at construction time still runs, with its cost. A named cdisc = vector with several lazy cards costs more on every verb (quadratic in the number of cards).
  • sv_read_cdisc() reads Dataset-JSON with the datasetjson package (checked against datasetjson 0.4.1, with column and dataset labels); if a file’s structure differs, it is skipped with a warning.
  • The row of labels is placed using one measurement of the header height; it could sit off only if a header later grows taller (for example after a late font load).
  • Checked in headless Chrome. viewer = "dialog" and "pane" were not checked in RStudio for this release.
  • Workspace files gain an optional view.labels_row field without a new schema version; older sideview versions ignore it.

sideview 0.4.0

Smaller items

  • Row cap for widgets. sideview_widget() and save_sideview() take max_rows = 5000. A longer data-frame table is cut to its first rows, its card says “First N of M rows” and one message names the tables cut (silent while knitting). max_rows = Inf embeds everything. Lazy tables are unchanged.
  • Positron. Without viewer =, sideview() and sideview_addin() open the browser in Positron, which has no dialog viewer; viewer = "dialog" there also opens the browser, with one message.
  • State files carry a schema version. sv_load_state() and state = read a file without a version as 0.2.0 and upgrade older files (stamped 0.3.0); a file from a newer sideview loads with one warning.
  • Install from r-universe: see the README.

Shiny module and proxy

  • sideviewUI() / sideviewServer() put an R-backed canvas into your own Shiny app, several per page. The server returns a proxy with the reactives code(), pipeline(), state() and cards(), and sideviewProxy(id) reaches the same canvas from elsewhere in the session. cards = can be a reactive; req() in it means “no cards yet”. Lazy (arrow / duckdb) cards in a module show their true size, not “First 500 of …”, because R serves the whole table.
  • Verbs: sv_add_card(), sv_replace_card(), sv_remove_card(), sv_set_state() and sv_highlight(), which pipe. A replace keeps the card’s place and size, re-checks the join keys, and disables, not deletes, any pipeline step that names a column the new table lacks (a mutate expression that uses it included), with one toast. A replace also keeps the card’s header sort and filter, so the canvas still agrees with the code.
  • Code execution is off in a module (Insert Script, Run & Exit, Run in R, Run Console). $code() is composed in the browser: treat it as untrusted text.
  • A module takes no AI settings from the browser, and shows the AI bar and the Copilot tab only when llm_fn is given.
  • The example app inst/examples/proxy/app.R has two canvases and a button for each verb. The gadget and the widget are unchanged.

Date-window joins

A join step can carry a date rule, so “labs within 7 days of the visit” is a join and not a hand-written filter. Click the calendar button on a join step to open the rule row. The shapes are Between (a date inside the other table’s start and end), Window (within a number of days before and after), Nearest before, Nearest after and Overlaps. Date, date-time and numeric columns work. The code uses join_by() and, for a window, two helper columns (.sv_lo, .sv_hi) that it drops again.

  • The join check knows the rule. The panel shows the rule and the rows it dropped (“Dropped by the rule”: rows that match on the key but not the rule), and the counts equal what dplyr returns. sv_join_diagnostics() has a new rule argument, and the gadget, the saved widget and duckdb/arrow cards all agree.
  • Strict (a checkbox on the join step) adds relationship = and unmatched = arguments taken from the join check, so the join stops with dplyr’s own error if the data changes under it. Strict is R-only for duckdb and arrow tables. The check looks at the two original tables, so Strict applies only to a join on them: when an earlier step on the left table changes its rows (a filter, another join, a summary, a pivot), or the right table has steps of its own, the checkbox is greyed with the reason, keeps its setting, and the code is the plain join.
  • Under a rule, na_matches = "never". sideview writes na_matches = "never" on every rule join (dplyr’s default would match NA to NA), so a key that is NA never matches another NA and the key check counts them the same way when a rule is set.
  • Saved workspaces keep the rule and the Strict flag. A workspace saved with a rule and opened in a 0.3.x install loses the rule silently (0.3.x ignores unknown fields).
  • Known differences. The saved widget drops fractions of a second from date-times, so a boundary that falls inside a second can differ from R. The generated duckdb code for a date-time window uses the session time zone when the ICU extension is loaded, so with a non-UTC TimeZone setting a boundary can move. Running the code in R on a mixed arrow/data-frame and duckdb chain may leave temporary dbplyr_* tables on your connection until it closes.
  • lubridate for duckdb date-time windows. On a duckdb table, the code for a window on a date-time column writes lubridate::days(), so run it with lubridate installed (it is in Suggests; Date and numeric windows do not need it).

Big tables: full data for arrow and duckdb cards

Arrow tables, datasets and queries and duckdb tables (dplyr::tbl()) used to keep only their first 50 rows, so a sort, a join check or a codebook looked complete when it was not. They now use the whole table.

  • Sort, filter and scroll run in duckdb on the whole table. The header shows the true row count.
  • Join check, column inspector and codebook profile the whole table in duckdb; only summaries come back into R, and the table is never collected. Results equal the in-memory ones. sv_join_diagnostics() accepts duckdb and Arrow tables, sv_column_profile() has a new column argument for them, and sv_codebook() accepts them and has a progress argument. Arrow tables go through a private duckdb connection that closes with the session.
  • The codebook has a new column, rows_profiled, after n. n is the table’s true row count and rows_profiled is how many rows the profile used. They are equal except for a preview-only card.
  • The canvas says what it used. Without duckdb, or when the link to a table is lost, the card header reads “First 50 of N rows” and the checks say “Based on the first 50 rows”. A toast explains a lost link, and a codebook shows its progress (“Profiling visits_db: column 40 of 200”).
  • Generated code stays lazy and ends in one collect(). Joins across duckdb, arrow and data frames are written so they run, a “contains” filter is stringr::str_detect(col, "<escaped literal>") (stringr is in Suggests), and a reshape on arrow collects first. If Run in R fails, the message adds “This step may need data in R: move collect() above it.”
  • Auto Map, the Discrepancy tab’s value comparison and the copilot’s schema summary still use the preview (the copilot is told the true row count). Auto Map suggestions and the discrepancy summary say so (“Based on the first 50 rows”), and so does the auto-clean button. Nothing is sent to the model but the schema.
  • Fixed: the gadget toolbar now has the Auto Map button (R answered the request, but there was no button). The saved widget drops it, since it needs R. When nothing is found, a toast says “No suggested joins found”.
  • Fixed: with duckdb 2.0, a >, >=, <, <= or = filter on an Arrow date-time column with a time zone matched no rows. duckdb 2.0 turns that comparison into a filter inside the Arrow scan, which loses every row.
  • Fixed: a BIGINT column (what duckdb gives count() and range()) made the lazy join check, filters and “contains” fail.
  • Fixed: an Arrow factor sorts by its levels, not its text, and keeps its class and its time zones in the gadget’s inspector and codebook.
  • Fixed: a filter value that is not a valid value for the column ("yes" on a logical, "abc" on a date) matches no rows, as on a data frame, instead of failing.
  • Fixed: card headers and printed cards write counts as 200,000, not 200000 or 2e+05; a widget codebook gives a lazy card’s true row count as n.
  • Fixed: a duckdb table whose name holds " or \ gets code that parses; a saved state never holds a card’s lazy table.
  • Sorted and scrolled windows on a big table are faster: duckdb returns only the rows shown (a sorted window of 5,000,000 rows takes under 0.3 s).

Known differences from an in-memory card:

  • “Contains” on a number matches its text. The grid filter drops a trailing .0, but in generated code duckdb writes a double as "130.0" where R writes "130", and float noise or scientific notation can differ.
  • A POSIXct value at exactly midnight, and -0, can print differently.
  • Join keys of different types compare as text; double keys compare exactly; an in-memory POSIXct key is compared as text where a database key is compared as an instant.
  • Arrow time-zone offsets are computed for 1900 to 2100, so local times outside that range may be off. duckdb TIMESTAMPTZ columns show in UTC. duckdb ordered factors report class "factor".
  • Joining arrow with duckdb copies the arrow side into a duckdb temporary table (arrow::to_duckdb() then dplyr::compute()), which uses memory. A data frame joined into duckdb is copied as sideview_<table>.
  • duckdb 1.4.3 can crash when it scans an arrow factor column that contains NA. sideview decodes these columns itself, but generated code that calls arrow::to_duckdb() on one may hit it: convert the factor to character first.
  • Two duckdb tables on different connections cannot be join-checked. A saved or embedded widget has no R session, so lazy cards there show the preview.

Other changes

  • The copilot chat keeps a reply in order: text written after the code now appears below the code instead of above it.
  • A join step in the Pipeline tab keeps its join type, move and delete buttons on one line in a narrow drawer; the key check stays on the line below.
  • The column inspector shows summary numbers to about four significant digits (5.338, not 5.33789). The profile and the codebook keep full precision.

sideview 0.3.0

A full pass over the user interface, tested in a real browser and in RStudio (dialog, Viewer pane, external browser, the addin, a saved HTML file and a Quarto page), plus new features for clinical data work.

New features

  • Pipeline with history. Each sort, filter, join, rename, recode, mutate, reshape or summarise is a step in the drawer’s Pipeline tab. Steps can be turned off, reordered or deleted, with undo/redo (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y) and a choice of %>% or |>. The drawer has real builder tabs: Join, Filter (several conditions, AND/OR), Arrange, Mutate, Recode, Reshape and Summarise.
  • Join diagnostics before you join. Connecting two columns shows the match rate in each direction, unmatched keys with examples, the key relationship (1:1, 1:m, m:m warning), rows produced by each join type, and NA, spacing or case problems in the keys. Also available as sv_join_diagnostics().
  • Column inspector and codebook. Click a column’s inspect icon for type, missingness, distinct values, a key check, summary statistics or top levels and a histogram. Export codebook writes a data dictionary for every card; sv_column_profile() and sv_codebook() do the same from R.
  • Save and open the workspace from the toolbar. sideview(..., state =) and sideview_widget(..., state =) restore card positions, zoom, sorts, filters, joins and the pipeline, and sv_load_state(launch = TRUE) now really launches.
  • Canvas navigation. A minimap (bottom-left; M hides it), Ctrl+K to find a card or column, and double-click a card title to zoom to it. Fit and Arrange buttons, and a tidy grid layout at launch.
  • Themes. theme = "auto" (follows RStudio or the browser), "light", "dark", sv_theme() or a bslib::bs_theme(). Every text colour meets WCAG AA contrast.
  • Keyboard and accessibility. Shortcuts (? lists them), real buttons with labels and visible focus rings, and the OS “reduce motion” setting is respected.
  • sv_llm_models() lists the models an Ollama or OpenAI-compatible server offers. AI errors now say how to fix them, and options(sideview.llm_think) controls Ollama reasoning models. See ?sideview for all options.

Bug fixes

  • viewer = "browser" works again. Closing or reloading the tab no longer leaves the console busy or kills the app (options(sideview.session_grace)).
  • Sort and filter now run on the full data, not just the first 500 rows shown. Sort code used %> instead of %>%.
  • Column headers stay put while a table scrolls, so splines stay attached. Maximize, minimize, fullscreen (including in the Viewer pane) and card resize now behave; the toolbar, palette, drawer and AI bar no longer overlap at any window size.
  • Click-to-connect no longer starts a stray second connection; sort/filter clicks no longer also connect columns; drawer tabs show their own content.
  • Done returns the generated code and Cancel returns NULL; “Run in R” keeps its result in a named object (sv_result by default), in the environment sideview() was called from (new env argument; the workspace when called from the console).
  • Card and column names are escaped everywhere, so odd names cannot break the page.
  • Recode and auto-clean emit dplyr::case_when() (case_match() is deprecated in dplyr 1.2).
  • A saved or embedded widget hides buttons that need an R session.
  • A widget in Quarto or R Markdown no longer stops the page from scrolling or restyles the host page.
  • Emoji icons are replaced by inline SVG icons that render the same everywhere.

Internal

  • One sideview-core HTML dependency with a content-based version, so browsers never use stale JavaScript or CSS. The bundled pan/zoom code is now honestly named sv-panzoom.js.
  • New real-browser test suite (tests/testthat/test-layout-browser.R, run with NOT_CRAN=true) checks layout and behaviour with real mouse and keyboard input.

sideview 0.2.0

Pillar 1: Big Data Scalability & CRAN Readiness

  • DOM Virtualization Engine: Added VirtualTable in sideview.js and sideview.css, bounding active table DOM nodes to ~30 rows with dynamic spacer elements and supporting 100k+ rows at 60 FPS scrolling.
  • Arrow & DuckDB Lazy Ingestion: Added zero-copy schema extraction methods (sv_normalize.arrow_table(), sv_normalize.Dataset(), sv_normalize.tbl_duckdb_connection()) with soft-dependency guards in Suggests:.
  • Multi-Key Composite Joins: Enhanced sv_code_join() and server reactivity to support vector keys (by = c("key1" = "key1", "key2" = "key2")) and relational multi-table pipeline chaining.

Pillar 2: Advanced Visual Wrangling & Profiling

  • Visual Pivoting Codegen: Added sv_code_pivot_longer() and sv_code_pivot_wider() with full syntactic backtick escaping and custom values_fn aggregation.
  • Group & Summarize Builder: Added sv_code_group_summarize() generating reproducible dplyr::group_by(...) %>% dplyr::summarise(..., .groups = 'drop') workflows.
  • Header Column Profiling: Embedded inline SVG 5-bin distribution sparklines (<svg class="sideview-sparkline">), categorical frequency distribution bars (.sideview-cat-profile), and color-coded missingness badges (.sideview-na-badge) with 25k-sample performance optimization.

Pillar 3: Canvas State Persistence & Cloud Sharing

  • State Serialization APIs: Added new_sideview_state(), sv_save_state(), and sv_load_state() supporting both portable .json and native R .rds workspace serialization for canvas pan/zoom, card coordinates, splines, and pipelines.

Pillar 4: Intelligent Copilot & Auto-Mapping

  • Heuristic Foreign Key Detection: Added sv_suggest_mappings() computing 3-part composite scores (name similarity with ID suffix detection, type compatibility, and Jaccard overlap) with precomputed unique sets and logical column exclusion.
  • Suggested Splines & Discrepancy Auto-Clean: Added animated dashed suggested splines (.sideview-spline-suggested dashMove) with click-to-accept join mapping, and sv_auto_clean_rules() / sv_code_auto_clean() for automatic dplyr::case_match() crosswalk synthesis.
  • Conversational AI Copilot Drawer: Added multi-turn chat tab with context retention (sv_build_chat_prompt()), turn-based history sliding window (20 turns), and active pipeline code guards.

Pillar 5: Automated Computer Use & GUI Verification

  • Automated GUI Test Suite: Added tests/testthat/test-computer-use-gui.R and headless DOM test runner gui-test-runner.js verifying 6 core interaction scenarios (canvas coordinates, dragging, port click / spline connect, suggested spline acceptance, sorting/filtering, drawer action dispatch) with diagnostic dumps in tempdir().

sideview 0.1.0

Recent Features & Enhancements

Interactive Canvas & Navigation

  • Dual Synchronized Scrolling: The sync scroll feature ([🔗] link icon in card headers) now synchronously locks both vertical rows (scrollTop) and horizontal columns (scrollLeft) in proportional lockstep across wide datasets.
  • Interactive Column Spline Disconnection:
    • Hovering over any connection spline displays a red highlight glow.
    • Direct click or right-click on any spline or connection port immediately removes the connection.
    • Shiny reactivity now dispatches column_disconnected to dynamically update code generation and downstream operations.
  • Port State Reset & Clearing: Enhanced clearOperations() to reliably purge active connecting port states (this.activePort) and strip visual .connecting classes when resetting the canvas.
  • Table Card Snapping & Dragging: Improved magnetic guideline alignment when dragging cards near each other.
  • Syntax Validation Suite: Added automated Node.js syntax parsing in tests/testthat/test-assets.R to ensure zero runtime script syntax errors.

Data Manipulation & Code Generation

  • Interactive Column Sorting:
    • Tri-state toggle on column header sort indicators (▲ Ascending, ▼ Descending, original).
    • Live in-memory row reordering across table cards.
    • Synthesizes and previews corresponding dplyr::arrange() pipelines in the Action Drawer.
  • Interactive Column Filtering:
    • Floating popover activated by column filter icon (🔍).
    • Supports numeric comparisons (>, >=, <, <=), exact matches (==, !=), and text substring filters (contains).
    • Filters rows in real time and synthesizes dplyr::filter() pipelines.
  • Non-Syntactic Identifier Escaping: Added client-side escapeColIdentifier() in sideview.js so column names with spaces or symbols (e.g. Patient ID, Glucose (mg/dL)) are safely wrapped in backticks across filter and arrange pipelines.
  • List-Column & Vector Safeguard: Hardened HTML grid table rendering in sideview_ui() to handle nested list-columns and vectors safely with a [list] placeholder, avoiding length > 1 evaluation errors under R 4.2+.

Action Drawer & Workflow Controls

  • Four Execution Modes:
    1. Insert Script: Pastes code at the current cursor location in the active RStudio script document via rstudioapi::insertText().
    2. Run & Exit: Sends code to the R console and closes the gadget immediately.
    3. Run in R: Evaluates code directly inside the current R environment (.GlobalEnv) with live row/column toast feedback.
    4. Run Console: Previews and buffers code for the RStudio console.
  • Clearing Controls:
    • Added a dedicated Clear button in the Action Drawer to reset all active splines, sort orders, and filters.
    • Added an [✓] Auto-clear toggle to automatically reset canvas interactions upon code insertion or copy.

LLM Assistance & Privacy Context

  • Local Ollama Integration: Full support for local models such as gemma4:26b and llama3.2 with zero data leakage (http://localhost:11434).
  • Cloud OpenAI-Compatible Support: Connect to OpenAI, OpenRouter, Groq, LM Studio, or vLLM.
  • Privacy-Safe Schema Synthesis: Prompts contain table names, column types, and high-level distribution ranges without exposing confidential raw records.

Testing & Verification

  • 705 Automated Tests: Full test suite across 9 contexts with 100% pass rate covering universal normalization, codegen, LLM prompts, RStudio bridges, reactive gadget events, HTML widgets, and static asset syntax.

sideview 0.1.0

  • Initial release of sideview: Multi-Table 2D Infinite Canvas for interactive data exploration, visual field mapping, and LLM-assisted Tidyverse code generation.
  • Universal S3 normalization engine (sv_normalize()) supporting data.frame, tibble, base::table, matrix, gt, flextable, and htmlwidgets.
  • Standalone self-contained HTML widget export via save_sideview().
  • Interactive Shiny Gadget and RStudio Addin (sideview(), sideview_addin()).
